title: Twelve years, 34 moments
lede: From one store in the Philadelphia suburbs to a liquidation run by its second owner. Filter by thread.

events.title: The first store opens
events.text: David Schlessinger, founder of Encore Books, incorporates Zany Brainy and opens a store in Wynnewood, Pennsylvania.

events.title: Fast openings begin
events.text: The company opens 11 stores in the year and ends it with 16. Sales are $23.5M and the loss is $6.7M.

events.title: The biggest early loss
events.text: Fifteen more stores open. Comparable-store sales rise 0.3% and the company loses $7.8M.

events.title: Vellios joins
events.text: Thomas G. Vellios arrives from Caldor as executive vice president of merchandising and marketing.

events.title: Spurgeon becomes chief executive
events.text: Keith C. Spurgeon, formerly of Toys “R” Us, takes over. The year ends with 43 stores and a $6.0M loss.

events.title: A slower year
events.text: Nine stores open, built to a smaller 10,600-square-foot prototype. The loss narrows to $153,000.

events.title: First profit
events.text: Net income of $9.0M on sales of $168.5M, including a $6.2M tax benefit. Twenty-three stores open, for 75 in all.

events.title: Initial public offering
events.text: 6.1 million shares are sold at $10.00 on Nasdaq under the symbol ZANY. The stock closes its first day at $11.44.

events.title: Internet joint venture
events.text: ZB Holdings is formed with Online Retail Partners to run zanybrainy.com. Each partner puts in $5.0M; the partner adds $10.0M in November.

events.title: A rival folds
events.text: Publishers Weekly reports the demise of Learningsmith, another educational toy chain.

events.title: Best year alone
events.text: Fiscal 1999 ends with 103 stores in 26 states, sales of $241.2M and net income of $6.9M.

events.title: More money for the website
events.text: The partners agree to put another $12.0M into the venture. Zany Brainy’s share is about $6.8M.

events.title: Noodle Kidoodle deal announced
events.text: An all-stock merger valued by the trade press at about $40M: 1.233 Zany Brainy shares for each Noodle Kidoodle share.

events.title: The merger takes effect
events.text: About 9.4 million shares are issued and 60 stores are added. The first $65.0M of a new $115M credit facility is completed the same day.

events.title: Spurgeon resigns
events.text: Vellios becomes acting chief executive.

events.title: The joint venture is dissolved
events.text: Zany Brainy takes full ownership of zanybrainy.com and assumes the venture’s liabilities.

events.title: The appraisal
events.text: The bank’s appraiser values the inventory at a level that significantly reduces what the company can borrow.

events.title: Fiscal 2000 ends
events.text: 188 stores in 34 states. Net sales of $400.5M, comparable-store sales down 10.0%, net loss of $80.7M.

events.title: Default asserted
events.text: The bank writes that the company has failed to comply with covenants. On March 9 it raises the interest rate to the default rate.

events.title: Suppliers agree to wait
events.text: The largest trade creditors form an informal committee and sign a two-week standstill. William Blair is hired to explore alternatives.

events.title: The website stops selling
events.text: Sales on zanybrainy.com are suspended “until further notice.”

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Zany Brainy and five subsidiaries file in Delaware with 187 stores and a $115M debtor-in-possession commitment from Wells Fargo Retail Finance.

events.title: Delisted
events.text: Nasdaq removes the stock, which had failed to hold a $1.00 bid.

events.title: Waterton agreement
events.text: The company announces a sale to Waterton Management that is expected to pay unsecured creditors 15 to 20 cents on the dollar.

events.title: The court picks The Right Start
events.text: The bankruptcy court rules that The Right Start’s offer is the highest and best. Shareholders will receive nothing.

events.title: Sale closes
events.text: A subsidiary of The Right Start takes over 187 stores in 34 states for consideration of about $100M. Zany Brainy’s own filing dates the closing to September 6.

events.title: The Right Start buys FAO Schwarz
events.text: The company soon renames itself FAO Inc. It now runs three chains.

events.title: The old company’s plan is confirmed
events.text: The court confirms a liquidating plan for Zany Brainy, Inc. All of its common shares are cancelled.

events.title: 55 closings announced
events.text: FAO Inc. says it will close 55 of its 169 Zany Brainy stores by March. The final number is 80.

events.title: FAO Inc. files for Chapter 11
events.text: The parent and four subsidiaries file in Delaware.

events.title: FAO Inc. emerges
events.text: It has closed 111 stores across its three chains. 89 Zany Brainy stores remain, in 27 states.

events.title: A warning and a default notice
events.text: FAO Inc. says sales are “disappointing and significantly below expectations.” Its lenders deliver a notice of default that afternoon.

events.title: Liquidation announced
events.text: FAO Inc. says it will file again, sell FAO Schwarz and The Right Start, and liquidate Zany Brainy. It files on December 4.

events.title: The name online
events.text: zanybrainy.com sells a small range of Zany Brainy-branded merchandise. The site names no operator.
